task.description: WF-03 step 7, TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, gate pass 1 of 3, the regression tests of the fix of ISS-0092 (REQ-110; run ISS-0092-20261117-01). Gate as WF-02 step 5b, and for a defect also: the new tests FAIL on the product before the fix and PASS after it. You cannot run the tests on this PC (decisions/0110), so prove everything with your own read-only scripts in your own folder and put what only GitHub can prove into result.must_be_proved_on_github. Do, in this order: (1) Read the whole test change (git diff HEAD -- tools/test and the new file tools/test/node-floor.test.js) and the designer's result. (2) Coverage table: every criterion of REQ-110 (and the numbered parts of the design section 10) → the test that goes red when it is violated; every entry point E1 to E11 of the design section 3 has a row; the hook rules of section 4; the single source of the floor and the equality (section 5); CI-3 and CI-8 (6.3, 6.4); anything without a test is a finding. (3) Soundness and independence: own oracles (a test does not import the rule it tests, except where the design makes the guard module the subject: say which test does and judge it); no dependence on the clock or the order; each test has its own data; no real home folder and no port 4780, 4781, 4782 or 4790; no secret; a test of a child process cannot hang the run (a timeout is set). (4) Mutants: apply at least 25 mutants of your OWN (not only the designer's 76) to copies of the product or of the rule functions, evaluated by your own independent harness (say what you reused); include: the floor constant changed in each of its places one at a time; the guard missing in each entry point one at a time; the guard placed after the dispatch; the version compare using string order or ignoring the patch part; a pre-release or an empty version accepted; engines text edited in the package file and in the lock root separately; check-latest removed, false, moved to another step; the hook accepting a version text with a shell metacharacter; the hook keeping a candidate's stderr; a candidate in a folder with a space; the header count changed. A surviving mutant is a finding unless proved equivalent. Prove the working tree is unchanged by your mutants (hashes before and after). (5) Defect rule: show which of the new tests are red on the product before the fix (a copy of the tree with the fix files at the state of the tag base/ISS-0092-20261117-01 and the new tests) and which stay green on purpose and why. (6) Nothing weakened: print the number of test( registrations and assert. occurrences of each changed file at the tag and now (not lower except where the replacement table says a row is replaced by stronger ones); no skip, todo or only. (7) The harness you rely on (a collector that replaces the node:test import): is it faithful for these tests; name what it cannot show. (8) Format and lint: run `npx prettier --check` and `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on the four changed files in a fresh clone of the project in your own folder (core.autocrlf=false, npm ci; they do not run the tests) and print the output. (9) Verdict PASS or FAIL with findings by severity; any item not passed is FAIL. Be economical: one script that applies all mutants and prints a table. RULES OF THIS PC (decisions/0110, 0127, 0129): do NOT run npm run check, cd app && npm run ..., node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; the record of a test run is read from GitHub with gh run view (read-only). Allowed: cd tools && npm run -s traces and handoffs-check; read-only git and gh; your own scripts and fresh clones (git clone -c core.autocrlf=false, npm ci) only in your own folder under <scratch>. Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). A server you start binds port 0 or a free high port and is stopped by its exact process id; never bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790. One browser at a time on this PC. No git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. LF line endings. Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). Fill only the result of your handoff; the top-level status stays PENDING and completed_at null: ORCH closes. English.

harness.what: own harness in <scratch>/iss92-07/h: shim.mjs (a collector that gets test(name, fn)), hooks.mjs (an ES resolve hook that maps the import of node:test to the collector, so no test file is edited), pre.mjs (runner process only: /bin/sh is mapped to the sh of Git for Windows, and a child that got SIGTERM reports code 0 as a Linux server does), runner.mjs (runs the named tests one by one with t.after), lib.mjs (tree copy, edit that fails when the pattern is not found, run), mutants.mjs (the table of 86), prefix.mjs (defect rule), series.mjs (series and load).

harness.faithful_for: the tests are plain functions with t.after and no subtests, mock, skip or timers of node:test (grep of t.<name>: only t.after), so a collector gives the same assertions and the same children; the red messages are the real assert messages.
harness.cannot_show: (1) Linux: the real /bin/sh (dash) for the hook rows, file modes, the real exit code 0 of a server after SIGTERM (emulated in my runner), POSIX paths; (2) the concurrency of node --test over many files and its load; (3) node:test's own handling of an uncaught exception or an unhandled rejection (my runner would end with no result, which I would have seen as NO RESULT); (4) the full npm run check and the e2e step; (5) the real Node of the runner (check-latest).

findings.place: tools/test/pixel-office-server.test.js, function rawHeadStatus and test SV-68; tools/test/node-floor.test.js, function rawHead and test NF-07
findings.what: Criterion 7 (and design 9.3) say the server answers 2 500 header lines with 431 AND CLOSES the connection. The helpers resolve on the 'close' event or after a 10 s timer that destroys the socket, and return only the status, so a server that answers 431 and leaves the socket open passes. Own mutants D05 (Pixel Office server) and D06 (team web server): a clientError handler that writes the 431 and does not end the socket; SV-68 and NF-07 stay green (the run only takes 10 s longer). The clause of the criterion has no assertion; a test that cannot fail for it is not a test (Q5).
findings.fix: In both helpers set a flag in the timer (timedOut = true before the destroy) and return closedByServer: !timedOut; in SV-68 and in NF-07 assert big.closedByServer === true for the 2 500-line probe (and, if wished, that the whole probe took under 5 s). Add D05 and D06 to the mutant table and run them.

findings.place: tools/test/node-floor.test.js, NF-05 rows of the programs without a help (cli.js E1, web/main.js E5, office-report.js E11)
findings.what: Design section 3 puts the guard as the first statement before the parsing of the arguments in these programs. All rows use a valid call, so a guard moved behind a pure parse survives: A-E5 (web/main.js after parseArgs), W-E1 (cli.js after the unknown-command check), W-E11 (office-report.js after parseArgs). The only visible difference is a wrong call below the floor: the usage line and code 2 instead of the refusal line; nothing is written either way, and README line 9 says a wrong call is answered as on any Node, so the harm is small. The designer's named limit (I1) is about reads, not about this.
findings.fix: Either add three twin rows under a simulated 22.21.1 (cli.js with an unknown command, web/main.js --port abc, office-report.js with an unknown option) that expect the refusal line and code 2 (design section 3, no help), or state in the design and in the README line the exact rule for a wrong call and name this as a limit in the report.

findings.what: The expected exit code of every refusal row is read from the imported constant. Mutant R07 (NODE_REFUSAL_EXIT = 3) is therefore green in NF-05c and red only in NF-04 (which pins the constant to 2). It is covered, but through one test; the end-to-end rows do not state the code themselves (AP-110).
findings.fix: Write the literal 2 in the rows (code: 2 as the default), keep NF-04's pin.

findings.what: Two hard-coded counts: a legitimate new node <file> script plus its row turns NF-05a red until the numbers are edited. The design says a later script adds its own row in the same run, so this is by design, but it is a second place to edit; the comparison of the script list with the rows already catches a missing row.
findings.fix: Optional: drop the two counts or keep them and name the rule in the test message ('edit the counts with the row').
